meaning: The number 74 has no prominent or well-established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
description: Unlike numbers such as 7, 12, 40 or 70, which carry deep symbolic resonance in the Bible and Jewish tradition, 74 is not a number attributed with special mystical or theological significance. It can be broken down into 70 + 4, where 70 symbolizes completeness (such as the 70 nations or the 70 years of exile) and 4 may represent the four corners of the earth, but this combination lacks an established history of interpretation. The number appears in Ezra 2:40 and Nehemiah 7:43, where it is stated that the Levites from the families of Jeshua and Kadmiel numbered 74 upon their return from exile in Babylon. Beyond this specific count, the number is not mentioned in any symbolically prominent way in the Bible or in central kabbalistic or rabbinic texts.

footnotes.text: The fact that the same number of Levites, 74, is given in both Ezra 2:40 and Nehemiah 7:43 strengthens the reliability of this census. Both texts reproduce lists of those who returned from the Babylonian exile under Zerubbabel, and the low number of Levites compared to the priests (4,289 according to Ezra 2:36–39) has been noted by biblical scholars as a sign that many Levites chose to remain in Babylon.
